children: Russia’s economy expanded by 1.3% in the second quarter of 2026, in line with preliminary estimates and recovering from a 0.2% contraction in the previous quarter.

The latest reading also marked the strongest growth since the first quarter of 2025, supported by a greater number of working days, improved external conditions and a fiscal boost, with government spending on the military and a temporary rise in oil revenues providing further support to the wartime economy.
Manufacturing grew 1.2%, while transportation and storage rose 4.0% and wholesale and retail trade increased 2.8%.
However, mining contracted 1.6%, while civilian industries remained under pressure.
For the first half of the year, GDP grew just 0.6%, half the pace recorded a year earlier, highlighting the economy’s sharp slowdown.
High interest rates, disruptions from Ukrainian drone strikes and weakness in civilian industries could limit the durability of the recovery.

title: Russian Economy Recovers in Q2
